app.name: DiCE-IFC
app.tagline: A BIM toolkit that never uploads your models
app.description: IFC viewing and federation, georeferencing, IDS authoring and validation, BCF management, and qualified signature with the Cartão de Cidadão. Everything is processed in your browser.
app.metaDescription: Browser-based BIM toolkit: IFC viewing and federation, georeferencing, IDS authoring and validation, BCF management, and qualified signature with the Cartão de Cidadão. Models never leave your device.

privacy.intro: This page is exhaustive on purpose. If DiCE-IFC ever sends something not listed below, that is a bug — please report it.
privacy.localTitle: Stays on your machine, but leaves the tab
privacy.localIntro: A browser cannot reach a smart card, so signing involves one hop out of the tab. It carries a hash and goes no further than loopback.

leaves.what: Dictionary search text, and the IFC class names your specification already mentions — IFCWALL, not any value
leaves.when: Only in the IDS editor, and only after you choose a bSDD dictionary. Nothing is selected by default
leaves.where: The buildingSMART Data Dictionary (api.bsdd.buildingsmart.org), via this app's API as a proxy
leaves.why: To suggest the property sets, property names and allowed values a class can carry, so a specification does not silently apply to nothing because of a typo. bSDD sends no CORS headers, so the call goes through this app's API — which also means bSDD sees this deployment's address rather than yours. Lookups fire on a class you have named, not on every keystroke. No model, no IDS file and no property value is sent, and the editor works normally with bSDD unreachable.

leaves.where: The configured tile provider. Self-hosted Protomaps by default, which is this app's own origin; this deployment is configured for OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org)
leaves.why: To draw a basemap under the model footprint in georeferencing. Tile requests reveal roughly where you are looking — in this module, that is where the building is — which is why a self-hosted provider is the default. OpenFreeMap needs no account and states that it does not log requests, but it is still a third party. Removing NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_STYLE_URL turns the basemap off; the georeferencing itself does not need it. When a MapTiler key is configured the panel also offers Streets, OpenStreetMap and Satellite from api.maptiler.com; those requests are tied to that account key. The basemap now covers whatever the camera is looking at, so panning and zooming out fetches tiles for the area you move to. Choosing 3D buildings streams 3D geometry from Cesium ion (api.cesium.com and assets.ion.cesium.com) against an ion token; those requests are tied to that token and ion's attribution stays on screen while the tiles are shown.

localOnly.what: A digest of the signature's own metadata — 32 to 64 bytes
localOnly.where: The DiCE-IFC signing companion, on http://127.0.0.1
localOnly.why: The signing key is on your Cartão de Cidadão, and a browser cannot talk to a smart card. The companion passes the digest to the card and returns the signature. It has no endpoint that accepts a document and refuses anything larger than a few kilobytes. Every request must carry a token the companion generates fresh each time it starts, and it hands that token out only to this application's own origin — which is why you never have to copy one, and why another web page cannot use it to drive your card.

never: IFC models — geometry, properties, quantities, classifications, everything
BCF issue sets, comments, viewpoints or snapshots
IDS specifications, whether authored here or imported
Validation results, reports and the entities that failed
Coordinates, control points or georeferencing parameters
Your signature PIN — the Autenticação.gov middleware asks for it, not this app
Your private key — it never leaves the Cartão de Cidadão
The signature value and the signed container
privacy.enforce1: Files are read with the File System Access API or drag-and-drop, parsed by WebAssembly inside Web Workers, cached in the Origin Private File System (a per-site sandbox that no other site and no server can read), and rendered by WebGPU or WebGL. All of that is browser-local by construction.
privacy.enforce2: On top of that, the codebase forbids passing a File, Blob or ArrayBuffer to any network call — a lint rule fails the build if someone tries — and a Content-Security-Policy blocks connections to origins other than this app's own origin, the configured map and 3D providers, and the signing companion on loopback. bSDD is reached through this app's own server rather than from the tab, so that service never sees your browser or your address. There is no account, no project database and no other backend: the app is a static front end.
privacy.enforce3: Signing works the same way. The document is hashed in the tab; only the hash of the signature's own metadata is handed to a local companion application, which passes it to the card through the Autenticação.gov middleware. The middleware asks you for the signature PIN directly — this app has no PIN field and never sees one. The signed container is assembled and zipped in the tab and saved straight to your disk.
privacy.enforce4: Clearing site data removes the OPFS cache and every draft stored with it.
privacy.metaDescription: Exactly which data DiCE-IFC sends over the network, and which data never does.
privacy.operatorText: {name} operates this deployment and is responsible for the processing described on this page. Contact:
privacy.rights: You have the rights the GDPR gives you over personal data held about you: access, rectification, erasure and objection, and the right to complain to a supervisory authority (in Portugal, the CNPD, cnpd.pt). The only personal data this deployment normally holds is what appears in server access logs.
privacy.serverText: Like any website, the server that delivers this application sees your IP address and the pages you request, and keeps ordinary access logs for security and fault-finding. They are kept by whoever operates this deployment, for the time their own policy states. They never contain a model, an issue set or a specification: those are never sent.
storage: One cookie, dice-locale, remembers whether you chose Portuguese or English. It is needed for that choice to stick and holds no identifier.
Browser storage keeps your theme, panel widths, clash matrix and saved settings, and draft work in the Origin Private File System. It stays in your browser; clearing site data removes it.
There are no analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.

filter.hint: Separate alternatives with commas. Use * as a wildcard, e.g. IfcWall*, or /regex/ for a pattern. Every filled field must match.

tolerances.title: Tolerances
tolerances.name: Name
tolerances.hint: A hard clash is ignored when the elements overlap by no more than the tolerance — how far one would have to move to clear the other, not how widely they touch, so a thin sliver along a wall joint does not count. With the volume option it is also ignored when the volume they share is smaller than the limit. Touching faces are never reported. A clearance rule reports elements closer together than its distance.

template.title: Residential building template
template.hint: A coordination baseline for a house or apartment block: architecture, structure, HVAC, plumbing, electrical, fire protection, ELV, lifts, site utilities and clearance zones, with 172 tests and their tolerances. Some groups share IFC classes and carry a note on what to filter. Replaces the current matrix; every group, tolerance and cell stays editable.

notes.a01: Architectural model only — leave out structural walls. It shares its classes with “Structural slabs & walls”, so separate them by source model or name.
notes.a02: Architectural model only (finishes, roof layers) — leave out the structural base slab. It shares its classes with “Structural slabs & walls”.
notes.a07: Fixed cabinetry and built-ins only. Filter by name or model: on its classes alone it selects all furniture and every proxy object.
notes.s01: Structural model only — permanent load-bearing solids. It shares its classes with the architectural walls and floors, so separate them by source model or name.
notes.h03: Hydronic and refrigerant systems only. Five groups select the same pipe classes: partition them by system or source model.
notes.p01: Potable cold, hot and recirculation systems only. Five groups select the same pipe classes: partition them by system or source model.
notes.p02: Sanitary, vent and rainwater systems only. Five groups select the same pipe classes: partition them by system or source model.
notes.f01: Sprinkler and suppression system only. Five groups select the same pipe classes: partition them by system or source model.
notes.c01: Underground wet services and site utilities only. Five groups select the same pipe classes: filter by site model or assigned system.
notes.z01: Selects only solids named CLZ_MAINT_*. Model each piece of equipment's approved maintenance envelope as such a solid; nothing is selected until you do.
notes.z02: Selects only solids named CLZ_EGRESS_*. Model the locally approved escape route and door swing as such solids; nothing is selected until you do.

reportPanel.verticalDatumNotSet: Not set — orthogonal heights have no stated reference.
reportPanel.siteDisagreementDetail: The IfcSite latitude/longitude is about {metres} m {direction} of the IfcMapConversion origin. Tools that read one or the other will show the model in different places.
reportPanel.notMappableHint: A map conversion and a projected CRS are needed before this model can be placed on a map or federated with confidence.

levels.20: Located — approximate latitude and longitude only
levels.30: Placed — site elevation and placement, but no orientation
levels.40: Oriented — true north is known, but there is no map conversion
levels.50: Fully georeferenced — map conversion and projected CRS

siteLatLongMissing.detail: The site declares no latitude or longitude.
siteLatLongMissing.remedy: Set the site's reference latitude and longitude, or georeference the model fully with an IfcMapConversion.

siteLatLongZero.detail: Latitude and longitude are both exactly 0°, which is a placeholder rather than a location.

siteLatLongRange.remedy: Check that the compound-degree values are correct.

elevationMissing.detail: No reference elevation, so heights are relative to the model origin only.
elevationMissing.remedy: Set the site's reference elevation above the vertical datum.

worldCoordinateSystemMissing.detail: The Model context declares no world coordinate system.
worldCoordinateSystemMissing.remedy: Not required, but an explicit identity placement documents the intent.

worldCoordinateSystemIdentity.detail: Identity — the model origin is the context origin.

trueNorthMissing.detail: The Model context declares no true north, so the model's orientation is unknown.
trueNorthMissing.remedy: Set TrueNorth on the Model representation context, or supply an IfcMapConversion, whose grid rotation supersedes it.

trueNorthZero.detail: TrueNorth is a zero-length direction, which carries no orientation.
trueNorthZero.remedy: Set a non-zero direction, e.g. (0, 1) when project north is true north.

mapConversionMissing.detail: No map conversion, so the model cannot be placed in a projected CRS.
mapConversionMissing.remedy: Add an IfcMapConversion with the eastings, northings and height of the model origin.

mapConversionPlaceholder.detail: Eastings and northings are both 0, which is a placeholder in every real projected CRS.
mapConversionPlaceholder.remedy: Set the real map coordinates of the model origin.

mapConversionScale.remedy: Confirm this is a deliberate grid scale factor and not a unit conversion that belongs in the project units.

projectedCrsMissing.detail: No projected CRS, so the map coordinates have no stated meaning.
projectedCrsMissing.remedy: Add an IfcProjectedCRS naming the EPSG code, e.g. EPSG:3763.

projectedCrsUnrecognised.detail: Name is “{name}”, which is not a recognisable EPSG code or a known CRS name.
projectedCrsUnrecognised.remedy: Name the CRS as an EPSG code so any tool can resolve it unambiguously.

controlPoints.fitPlacementHint: At least two points are needed to solve rotation and scale
controlPoints.noneYet: No control points. Add at least two pairs — a point in the model and the same point as surveyed — to solve the placement.

signSetup.title: Signing setup
signSetup.description: What has to be installed on this machine before a Cartão de Cidadão can sign.
signSetup.cmdNotSupportedTitle: Chave Móvel Digital is not supported
signSetup.cmdNotSupportedBody: This application signs with the physical Cartão de Cidadão only. Chave Móvel Digital is a remote signing service: using it would mean sending a digest of your model off this machine, which is exactly what this application is built not to do. To sign with CMD, use the official Autenticação.gov desktop application instead.
signSetup.signingCompanionBody: A browser cannot talk to a smart card, so a small local program does it. Install it once; it starts with you and this page pairs with it by itself. There is nothing to copy.
signSetup.noInstallerPublished: No installer is published for this deployment. Build one with companion/packaging/build_macos.sh or build_windows.ps1, or run it from source with pip install ./companion && dice-companion. See companion/packaging/README.md.
signSetup.companionDigestOnly: The companion signs a digest and nothing else — your model never reaches it, and neither does your PIN, which the card middleware asks for in its own window.
signSetup.cardReaderBody: Any CCID reader. A CC v2 can also be read contactlessly, which needs the CAN printed on the card.
signSetup.middlewareBody: Provides pteidpkcs11, the PKCS#11 module that talks to the card. It raises its own PIN window — this application never sees, transports or stores your PIN.
signSetup.extensionBody: A browser cannot reach a smart card: WebCrypto has no token access and WebAuthn cannot drive a qualified signing key. A locally installed companion is unavoidable.
signSetup.statusUnknown: — cannot be detected from the browser
signSetup.noProviderRemedy: No signing provider could be loaded in this browser.

warning.macos: Not signed by Apple yet, so macOS will say “unidentified developer”. Right-click the downloaded file and choose Open.

windows.installer: Not code-signed yet, so SmartScreen will warn on first run. Choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.
windows.program: The program itself, not an installer: run it and keep it running (it does not start with Windows yet). Not code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn on first run — choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”.

middleware.label: Autenticação.gov middleware (pteid)
middleware.remedy: Install the Autenticação.gov application — it provides the PKCS#11 module the card needs.

reader.label: Smart card reader
reader.remedy: Connect a card reader, or use a contactless reader with the card's CAN.

card.label: Cartão de Cidadão
card.remedy: Insert the card into the reader.

notPaired.remedy: The companion is running but did not pair. Update it — versions before {version} have no /pair endpoint and needed a token pasted by hand.

signVerify.title: Verify a signature
signVerify.description: Drop a signed container to re-hash its payload and check the signature. Nothing is uploaded.

signVerify.onlyOne: Only one container is checked at a time — checking {name}.
signVerify.signatureValid: Signature valid — the content is exactly what was signed
signVerify.notATrustDecision: This is not a trust decision. It proves the content has not changed since it was signed, and that the signer held the key for the certificate below. Whether that certificate is a genuine Portuguese qualified certificate, and whether it had been revoked, needs the trusted list and an OCSP responder — data a browser cannot fetch directly. That check is not implemented yet.

signModule.perFileModeHint: One PIN entry per file. Each file gets its own container that can be verified, and sent, entirely on its own.
signModule.pinInOwnWindow: The card middleware is asking for your signature PIN in its own window. This application never sees it.

about.metaDescription: Licence, third-party credits, data attributions and disclaimers for DiCE-IFC.
about.title: About, credits and licences
about.intro: DiCE-IFC is a browser-based BIM toolkit. This page says what it is built on, whose data it can show, and what you should not take it to promise.

licence.title: Licence
licence.body: DiCE-IFC is free software, released under the MIT licence: you may use, copy, modify and distribute it, provided the copyright and licence notice are kept. It comes with no warranty.

thirdParty.title: Open-source software
thirdParty.intro: DiCE-IFC is built on the software below, and on several hundred smaller packages. Each remains under its own licence.
thirdParty.fullList: Licence texts for every package this application ships (text file)
thirdParty.mpl: The IFC-Lite packages (@ifc-lite/*) are licensed under the Mozilla Public License 2.0. They are used unmodified, and their source is available from the project's repository.

roles.ifclite: Reads and writes IFC, BCF and IDS; builds model geometry
roles.libxml2: Validates XML against the buildingSMART schemas

data.title: Data and services
data.intro: Some features can show data from other providers. All of it is optional and off until you switch it on; what is sent to them is listed on the privacy page.

osm.name: OpenStreetMap
osm.text: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Map data is available under the Open Database Licence (ODbL). Shown with OSM buildings and in OpenStreetMap-based imagery and basemaps.

openfreemap.name: OpenFreeMap
openfreemap.text: Basemap tiles, when configured: OpenFreeMap © OpenMapTiles, data from OpenStreetMap.

maptiler.name: MapTiler
maptiler.text: Streets, OpenStreetMap and satellite imagery, when a MapTiler key is configured: © MapTiler © OpenStreetMap contributors. Subject to MapTiler's terms.

cesium.name: Cesium ion and Cesium World Terrain
cesium.text: Terrain and OSM buildings are streamed from Cesium ion, and its credit stays on screen while they are shown. Used under Cesium ion's terms of service.

google.text: Only when selected. Provided by Google and subject to the Google Maps Platform terms of service, including their attribution and usage conditions.

egm96.name: EGM96 geoid
egm96.text: Used to convert between orthometric and ellipsoidal heights. Derived from the public-domain model of the U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency; approximate (a 1° grid) and not for survey-grade work.

epsg.name: EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset
epsg.text: Coordinate reference system definitions, © IOGP (epsg.org). Provided without warranty.

buildingsmart.name: buildingSMART
buildingsmart.text: IDS and BCF schemas and the buildingSMART Data Dictionary. Each dictionary has its own licence, shown on bSDD. IFC, BCF, IDS and bSDD are names of buildingSMART International; this application is not endorsed by or affiliated with it.

items.title: No warranty
items.text: This software is provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind, as the MIT licence states. Its operators are not liable for any loss arising from its use.

items.title: Results are an aid, not a certification
items.text: Clash detection, IDS validation, georeferencing checks and quantity queries depend on the models they are given and on the settings chosen. Check results before relying on them for design, contractual or safety decisions.

items.title: Georeferencing accuracy
items.text: Coordinate transformations use proj4 and the EPSG definitions credited above. Systems that need a datum-shift grid are not offered, and heights use a coarse geoid grid. Do not use it for survey-grade or legal-boundary work.

items.title: Digital signatures
items.text: A valid result means the content is exactly what was signed and that the signer held the private key for the certificate enclosed in the container. It does not show that the certificate is trusted, was valid when used, or has not been revoked, and these signatures carry no trusted timestamp. Whether a signature has legal effect depends on the applicable law and the format required; take legal advice where it matters. Signing needs your own Cartão de Cidadão, its signature PIN and the Autenticação.gov middleware, none of which this application includes. It never sees your PIN.

items.title: The signing companion
items.text: A small program you install yourself on your own computer. It is not code-signed yet, so macOS and Windows warn before running it; the setup page explains why.

items.title: No affiliation or endorsement
items.text: Cartão de Cidadão and Autenticação.gov belong to the Portuguese State and AMA; buildingSMART, IFC, BCF and IDS to buildingSMART International; Google, MapTiler, Cesium and OpenStreetMap to their owners. They are named to say what this application works with, and none of them endorses it. The ISISE and University of Minho logos belong to those institutions.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.text: The interface is built from accessible components and its controls carry text labels, but it has not been formally audited against WCAG. The 3D viewport needs a pointer; the model tree and the lists offer a keyboard route to select and inspect elements.
